newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil launches export credit agency.
newsitem.headline: Brazil launches export credit agency.

text.p: Banco do Brasil's investment arm, BB Investimentos, four Brazilian insurers and France's export guarantee agency Coface have launched an export credit agency, a Banco do Brasil official said.

The new private company, Seguradora Brasileira de Credito a Exportacao, located in Rio de Janeiro will open for business in July with a starting capital of 10 million reais ($9.34 million), said Banco do Brasil's Carlos Eduardo Andrade, who is responsible for developing the project.

"The objective of the company is to insure export operations which correspond to 12 percent of Brazil's total exports," Andrade said. "We will start off by insuring around two percent of total Brazilian exports and in six years time we aim to reach 12 percent."

The company will insure Brazilian exports against commercial risks of up to two years, as well as against political and extraordinary risks, Andrade said. The export credit agency will cover its risks in the international re-insurance market.

BB Investimentos and the four Brazilian insurers -- Bradesco, HSBC Bamerindus, Sul America, Minas Brasil -- will each have an 11 percent stake in the company, while Coface will hold 25 percent. The remaining 20 percent will go to new shareholders.

Andrade said the government expected the new export insurer, which would mainly benefit medium to small size exporters, to boost Brazilian sales abroad by 500 million reais ($467.3 million) a year and help contain the country's booming trade deficit.
Brazil's trade gap hit $5.54 billion last year and is set to top $11 billion by the end of 1997.

Coface's role in the new export insurance partnership is one of technology transfer, said Andrade. Coface has a databank containing information on more than 20 million exporters in 43 countries across the world that can provide information on a given export transaction within 24 hours.
"The great advantage (of the new insurer) for the Brazilian exporter is the level of information at his disposal," Andrade said.
He said the insurance partners still had to decide whether to list Seguradora Brasileira de Credito a Exportacao on the Brazilian stock exchange.
